experimental_procedure: 4.9. Continuous-Flow DIBAL-H Reduction of a Methyl Ester to the Aldehyde. Procedure for the Flow Preparation of Garner's Aldehyde (tert-Butyl (4S)-4-Formyl-2,2-dimethyl-1,3-oxazolidine-3-carboxylate) (11) from the Methyl Ester. Garner's methyl ester (10) of >95% purity was prepared from L-serine in three steps from a literature procedure.44 The reactors were constructed according to Scheme 6 and consisted of a cooled reactor assembly equipped with three reagent precooling PFA loops of 0.4 mL volume, a PFA reactor coil of 10 mL volume, and a 0.4 mL cooled PFA quench loop. This reactor assembly was maintained at -70 °C. In series with this reactor was a PFA reactor coil of 2 mL volume at ambient temperature (23-26 °C) and a back-pressure regulator with a 6 bar limit. The system was prepared according to the general procedure above and the cooled reactor allowed to stabilise at its set-point temperature before the reaction was begun. Whilst the system was being prepared, 150 mL of a 0.5 M solution of methyl ester 10 in anhydrous toluene, in an argon-purged flask, and 350 mL of a 2.0 M solution of anhydrous methanol in anhydrous toluene, in a separate argon-purged flask, were prepared. The solution of methyl ester was plugged into line A and the solution of methanol to line C. A solution of diisobutylaluminium hydride (DIBAL-H), 1.0 M nominal concentration in hexane, was plugged into line B. The three pumps were begun, pumping solvent at the indicated flow rates for 5 min. Then, line A was switched to pump reagent, and 10 min timed. Line B and C were then switched to pumping reagents. A further 35 min were timed after which the output stream beyond the BPR was allowed to drip into stirring 300 mL of saturated aqueous Rochelle's salt (sodium potassium tartrate) solution kept under argon at room temperature. A total of 8 h of collection was timed, after which the output was transferred back to waste, and the three lines switched to pumping solvent simultaneously. The clean-down procedure for the system was then begun. The biphasic output was diluted with diethyl ether (300 mL) and water (50 mL), and the mixture was stirred vigorously under argon for 1 h. After this time, the stirring was halted, and the biphasic system was allowed to settle, at which time two clean phases formed. The phases were separated, the aqueous phase was extracted with diethyl ether (4 × 100 mL), the combined organic phases were dried over magnesium sulfate and concentrated in vacuo.
